subject: A 6.4-to-7.8-hour sleep window tracked slower biological aging
script: From Agewell Brief: A 6.4-to-7.8-hour sleep window tracked slower biological aging. New research suggests a specific sleep duration range could be linked to slower biological aging. Here's what to make of the findings. Sleep is a cornerstone of health, yet many older adults struggle to get enough. This new research offers a concrete target: 6.4 to 7.8 hours per night. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
